problems.stem: Which evidence trace would make this artifact easiest to review and improve?
options: The artifact is visually polished and complete.
You identify a claim, evidence source, bounded support move, accepted suggestion, rejected suggestion, and revision.
The learner uses AI for every step so the artifact is consistent.
The learner writes a generic reflection after submitting.
problems.explanation: Strong evidence shows your judgment and a traceable revision decision.

problems.stem: Which annotation would help BigAL give targeted support?
options: I am confused about which constraint should override the AI suggestion in this artifact.
problems.explanation: A useful annotation tells BigAL what concept, constraint, or decision needs attention.

problems.stem: What is the strongest AI-use boundary for this section?
options: Ask AI to complete the artifact and submit it.
Use AI for one bounded critique or revision option, then judge it against course evidence.
Avoid AI even when the assignment asks for critique.
Use AI only to make the artifact sound more polished.
problems.explanation: The learner remains responsible for judgment; the tool provides bounded support.

problems.stem: Which detail would make later support more useful?
options: Your confidence, question type, support request, practice result, and revision quality.
Only the number of words in the note.
problems.explanation: Useful support depends on visible evidence, not only completion.
